title: Optimization of 14-Layer All-Dielectric Polarizing Beam Splitter
scientific_hypothesis: A 14-layer stack offers the highest flexibility among the considered options, enabling the design of a broadband polarizing beam splitter with superior performance metrics (higher TE R, higher TM T) and potentially wider bandwidth, albeit at the cost of increased complexity and thickness.
design_principle: Use the extended number of layers to approximate an ideal anti-reflection coating for TM polarization and a high-reflectivity mirror for TE polarization simultaneously. This may involve chirped layer thicknesses or complex multi-cavity structures to flatten the spectral response.
proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica
manufacturing_considerations: Highest fabrication complexity among the three options
Longest deposition time and highest risk of cumulative thickness errors
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory for polarizing beam splitters
Transfer Matrix Method (TMM) for planar multilayer systems
Refractive index dispersion data for TiO2 and SiO2 in visible spectrum
expected_advantages: Best possible performance metrics (highest TE R, TM T) due to maximum degrees of freedom
Widest operational bandwidth and flattest spectral response
known_risks: Most sensitive to manufacturing tolerances due to high complexity
Diminishing returns on performance improvement relative to added cost and complexity
Total thickness may approach limits of stress management in thin films
execution_request_english: Perform a numerical optimization of a 14-layer all-dielectric polarizing beam splitter on a fused silica substrate. Incident medium: Air. Substrate: Fused Silica. Incidence angle: 45 degrees. Wavelength range: 500-650 nm. Materials: TiO2 and SiO2 for the coating layers. Stack sequence: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Design variables: Thicknesses of all 14 coating layers, bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm. Objective: Maximize a composite score that rewards Mean TE Reflectance (target >= 90%) and Mean TM Transmittance (target >= 85%), while penalizing total physical thickness. After finding the optimal thicknesses, perform a robustness analysis by simulating the response with independent normally distributed layer-thickness errors (sigma = 1.5% of nominal thickness) and a common incidence-angle offset uniformly distributed between -1 and +1 degree. Report the optimal thicknesses, the mean TE reflectance, mean TM transmittance, total thickness, and the statistical distribution of performance under uncertainty. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 45 degrees. polarization s, p. wavelength intervals 500-650 nm. soft objectives: high TE reflectance (mean >= 90%); high TM transmittance (mean >= 85%); fewer layers; lower total thickness. robustness conditions: layer thicknesses bounded between 25 nm and 220 nm; total layer counts restricted to 6, 10, or 14.
